name: Inverters (DC to AC)
summary: Inverters turn battery DC (12, 24 or 48V) into mains AC to run normal appliances.
uses: Running mains tools, chargers and lights from batteries
The heart of a solar power system
Backup power for medical devices and fridges (pure sine is best)
identify: Finned car and RV inverters with a cigarette plug or battery leads; bigger units in RVs, boats, cabins, solar sheds and telecom huts. Every UPS holds an inverter and a battery. Labels say pure or modified sine and give watts.
test: Connect to a charged battery with thick cables and run a small load like a lamp. A beeping alarm usually means low battery or overload. The output is lethal mains voltage, and big units hold charge after switch-off.
